answer: In an attestation graph, trust propagates through bounded-length random walks, limiting how far endorsements can carry influence. A sybil cluster may be dense internally, like a mesa, yet connect to honest participants through only a sparse cut. Its low conductance restricts random-walk flow across that boundary; min-cut and transitivity bounds therefore cap its aggregate voting weight. Comparing the cut with a mirror partition helps separate genuine independent trust—an oasis—from fabricated density.
